segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: Hello Mrs. Johnson, this is Dr. Smith. How are you feeling today?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: Hi Dr. Smith. I've been having some trouble with my blood pressure lately. It was 140/90 yesterday when I checked it at home.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: I see. That's a bit elevated. Have you been taking your medications regularly?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: Yes, I've been taking my lisinopril every day as prescribed. I'm also taking metformin for my diabetes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: Good. What about your blood sugar levels? Have you been monitoring those?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: Yes, my glucose was 130 this morning. That's better than last week when it was around 150.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: That's an improvement. I'm glad to see your glucose is coming down. How about your diet and exercise?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: I've been trying to eat better. I'm having more vegetables and less processed food. I'm also walking for about 20 minutes every day.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: That's excellent progress, Mrs. Johnson. I recommend increasing your walking to 30 minutes daily if possible. It would help with both your blood pressure and blood sugar control.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: I think I can do that. I'm feeling a bit better overall, but I'm still having some headaches occasionally.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: I'm concerned about those headaches. They could be related to your blood pressure. I suggest you monitor your blood pressure when you have a headache to see if there's a correlation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: That makes sense. I'll do that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.transcription: Great. Let's schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to check your progress. In the meantime, continue with your medications, increase your walking to 30 minutes daily, and keep monitoring your blood pressure and glucose.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.transcription: Thank you, Dr. Smith. I'll see you in 2 weeks.
